I am 51 years old, and I have farmed these 16.9 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. I finished middle school, so I can read a fertilizer bag and I talk to the input dealer in town, but mostly I go by what I have seen work with my own eyes and what my neighbors do. My household is just my wife and me. We both do off-farm work when we can get it, so for the heavy jobs on 16.9 mu I hire machinery services. With this much land, I have to think about my whole budget and be efficient, but I can also absorb a small loss if the weather turns bad.

It is March now, and the winter wheat I planted last October is turning green. Here is what I will do this year.

For the wheat: I sowed an improved variety — the same kind most people around here plant, what the seed dealer calls a high-yield line. Last autumn at sowing, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg of the 15-15-15 type. That gave me my base phosphorus and potassium. This spring I will topdress with urea twice: at green-up, I will spread half a bag, 25 kg per mu, and at jointing stage another 10 kg per mu. In total that comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu for the whole wheat season. The phosphorus and potassium from autumn are enough, about 6 kg P and 5 kg K per mu. I will irrigate three times from now until harvest: green-up water in March, jointing water in April, and grain-filling water in May. I pump from my well. I will spray pesticide twice — once for weeds and once later for aphids and disease when it warms up. I expect about 550 kg per mu if we do not get a late frost.

For the summer maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize seed. Everyone uses hybrids now — you cannot get good yield without them. I hire the no-tillage seeder that comes right behind the combine harvester. It saves time and labor, which matters since my wife and I cannot do everything ourselves. At planting I will put down about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. Then when the maize reaches the big trumpet stage, I will topdress with 30 kg per mu of urea. Total nitrogen for maize will be about 20 kg per mu, phosphorus about 5 kg, potassium about 5 kg. I will irrigate twice if the rain is not enough — once after emergence and once at jointing. Summer rains usually help. I will spray twice: herbicide at seedling stage and insecticide for corn borer. I expect about 650 kg per mu.

I watch my costs carefully. Spending more on fertilizer means less cash for pesticide or hired labor. But I would rather put a bit too much fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money I spent for insurance. I watch what my neighbors do — if everyone around me applies roughly this much, then I do the same. Change is risky, and I only change when I see it work on someone else's field first.
